title: Grade 4 French — Wed, Jun 25
description: Le temps et les saisons — Day 3 of 5: Les quatre saisons (The four seasons)
subject: french

questions.question: How do you say 'the four seasons' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Les quatre saisons' = the four seasons. 'Saison' (feminine, plural: saisons). 'Quatre' = four.

questions.question: Which season comes after 'l'été' (summer) in France?
questions.explanation: The sequence: le printemps (spring) → l'été (summer) → l'automne (autumn) → l'hiver (winter). After summer comes autumn.

questions.question: How do you say 'In summer, the weather is hot' in French?
questions.explanation: 'En été, il fait chaud.' ✓ 'Été' = summer. Use 'en' with all seasons EXCEPT 'printemps' which uses 'au' (au printemps).

questions.question: 'Au printemps' means:
questions.explanation: 'Au printemps' = in spring. Printemps uses 'au' (not 'en') because it is a masculine noun. The others use 'en': en été, en automne, en hiver.

questions.question: In France, which season is known for colourful leaves and harvest?
questions.explanation: 'L'automne' (autumn/fall) — leaves turn red, orange and gold; harvest time. In French, 'les feuilles tombent' (the leaves fall) is a classic autumn description.

questions.question: Complete: 'En hiver, ___ et ___ souvent.'
options: il fait chaud et il pleut
il fait froid et il neige
il fait beau et il y a du soleil
il fait frais et il y a des fleurs
questions.explanation: 'En hiver, il fait froid et il neige souvent.' = In winter, it is cold and it often snows. 'Souvent' = often. Classic winter weather description.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'Spring has flowers and mild weather'?
options: Au printemps, il y a des fleurs et il fait doux.
En printemps, il y a des fleurs.
questions.explanation: 'Au printemps, il y a des fleurs et il fait doux.' ✓ 'Des fleurs' = flowers. 'Il fait doux' = the weather is mild/pleasant. Note 'au' (not 'en') with printemps.

questions.question: Match the season with its French description. 'Les enfants jouent à la plage et vont en vacances.'
questions.explanation: 'Les enfants jouent à la plage' (children play on the beach) 'et vont en vacances' (and go on holiday) — this is classic summer (l'été) activity in France.

questions.question: Spot the grammar error: 'En hiver, il fait du neige et il fait froid.'
options: 'il fait du neige' — should be 'il neige' (neiger is an impersonal verb, not 'faire + du neige')
questions.explanation: 'Il fait du neige' is incorrect. Snow uses the verb 'neiger': 'il neige.' (Never 'il fait du neige'.) Correct sentence: 'En hiver, il neige et il fait froid.'

questions.question: France has 4 seasons. In India, we often describe a different seasonal pattern. How would you say 'In India, there is a rainy season' in French?
options: En Inde, il y a une saison des pluies.
En Inde, le printemps est long.
questions.explanation: 'En Inde, il y a une saison des pluies.' = In India, there is a rainy season. 'Une saison des pluies' = a rainy season (monsoon). 'En Inde' = in India.

questions.question: Why does French use 'au printemps' but 'en été / en automne / en hiver'?
options: 'Printemps' is masculine, so 'en' + le = 'au' (contraction). The other seasons are also masculine but 'au' is used only with printemps by convention in some analyses; in practice: au printemps is the fixed form and en is used for the rest.
questions.explanation: The rule is simply: 'au printemps' (fixed expression) and 'en été/en automne/en hiver'. Students must memorise this usage. The preposition difference is a fixed grammatical feature of French seasonal expressions.

questions.question: Seasonal description: 'Les arbres perdent leurs feuilles et les jours raccourcissent.' Which season?
questions.explanation: 'Les arbres perdent leurs feuilles' (trees lose their leaves) and 'les jours raccourcissent' (the days get shorter) — both are characteristic of 'l'automne' (autumn).

questions.question: Write a full description of spring in French: best choice?
options: Au printemps, il fait doux, les fleurs poussent et les oiseaux chantent.
Au printemps, il fait très froid.
Au printemps, il y a du brouillard partout.
questions.explanation: 'Au printemps, il fait doux (mild), les fleurs poussent (flowers grow) et les oiseaux chantent (birds sing).' This is accurate, rich and grammatically correct.

questions.question: Order the seasons starting from the coldest to the hottest: ___, ___, ___, ___
questions.explanation: Coldest → hottest: l'hiver (winter, coldest) → le printemps (spring, mild) → l'été (summer, hottest) → l'automne (autumn, cooling). Note: l'automne is placed last as it cools down from summer.

questions.question: Complete all four season descriptions: 'Au printemps ___, en été ___, en automne ___, en hiver ___.'
options: il neige / il fait froid / il fait beau / il fait chaud
il fait doux / il fait chaud / les feuilles tombent / il neige
il pleut / il fait beau / il fait froid / il fait doux
il fait chaud / il neige / il fait doux / les fleurs poussent
questions.explanation: Au printemps il fait doux ✓. En été il fait chaud ✓. En automne les feuilles tombent ✓. En hiver il neige ✓. Each description is the most typical/characteristic for that season in France.
